LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  August 22, 2023

1. A meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by Chair
  Crosby at 6:30 p.m.

  Executive Board Members present:

  Executive Board
  Rick Crosby, YFAC Chair, Council Member
  Wendy Lau, YFAC Vice Chair, Mayor Pro Tem
  Denise Fisher, Resident

  Jason Prows, LVPD
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Nikole Burgess, BUSD
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne
  Erin Beilstein, City of La Verne
  Robin Carder, Resident
  Emily Turner, Resident
  Luke Melkesian, Resident

2. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the June 27, 2023, meeting were
  approved.

3. SRO Report  With a few days into the school year, there have been
  no incidents or issues for the School Resource Officer.
  Lieutenant Prows shared that there have been extra
  officers and personnel on campus during drop off and
  pick up to ensure a safe start to the year.

4. BUSD Welcome Back  Mark Rodgers shared that there have been no major
  issues with the start of the school year. The district is
  seeing enrollment at a higher level than pre-Covid
  levels, with multiple grade levels almost at capacity.
  The TK class is approximately 440 students as the
  program continues to grow and expand per state
  regulations. The district has been sharing a lot of
  information with the parents and community including
  at Back to School Night.

5. Finance Update  Assistant City Manager JR Ranells shared that YFAC
  is funded completely through donations. The last
  fundraiser was approximately 5 years ago, and the
  committee has continued to do programs, but has not
  increased funds or donations. The majority of the
  funding was spent with the summer lunch program
  that saw record numbers and unanticipated success
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes August 22, 2023, page 2

  this summer. As a result, YFAC is unable to support
  the School Counseling program. However, this year
  YFAC will not be charged for its portion of the School
  Counseling program through Tri-City Mental Health as
  BUSD will be covering YFAC’s share.

6. Summer Lunch Program  Assistant City Manager JR Ranells shared with the
  group that the summer lunch program saw about triple
  the number of students from previous years. It cost
  $18,000 for lunches this past summer with a total of
  over 3,000 students served. The Tri-City grant that
  YFAC received for $7,000 does not cover the program
  cost, so the committee will use the remainder of the
  YFAC budget to cover the cost of the program.

7. 501c3 Designation  Following the presentation regarding the YFAC budget,
  Assistant City Manager JR Ranells shared that the
  partnership with Dan Harden’s foundation, The Reed
  Foundation, will be beneficial for long-term
  sustainability of the committee. City staff submitted the
  501c3 application to the IRS and the hope is that in
  September the Ruth Reed Foundation could provide us
  funding if the 501c3 goes through. Executive Board
  Member Denise Fisher asked if YFAC is able to have
  another committee that is designated as a 501c3
  receive the funds and then transfer them to YFAC.
  Council Member Wendy Lau inquired about the
  parameters on the donations given through the Reed
  Foundation and what kinds of programs YFAC would be
  executing.

8. Public Comment  Resident Luke Melkesian shared that he is looking to
  bring a curriculum to the high school level regarding
  the increase in human trafficking and would like to
  partner with outside agencies and the school district to
  bring this education and awareness to the community.

9. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting was scheduled for September
  26, 2023.

10. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:20 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

Erin Beilstein
Management Analyst
